notes: N097. BSCCM: how well can every pair of cell lineages be told apart from the PREDICTED markers (N085 record ensemble)? Scale: for lineages A and B with defining markers a and b, every cell gets the score z(predicted a) - z(predicted b) (z-score over all test cells); the tile is the AUROC of that score for A cells vs B cells = the probability that a randomly drawn A cell scores higher than a randomly drawn B cell. .5 = coin flip (not separable), .7 = weak, .8 = moderate, .9 = good, 1 = perfect. No classifier is fitted; the matrix is symmetric. Lineages = positives of each marker on its own single-stain slide of the TEST draw. a train draw 1 -> test draw 0 (T vs B .95), b train draw 0 -> test draw 1 (T vs B .70; only 10 B cells), c mean of a and b (T vs B .82; range .82-.99). Slide control (ALL cells of slide a vs ALL cells of slide b, same score; same blood draw -> expected .5): mean |AUROC - .5| = 0.040, range 0.40-0.54.
significance: two-sided; Holm-corrected over all comparisons of a panel (one family per panel); * <0.05 ** <0.01 *** <0.001 **** <0.0001
